stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan recovery: Kalinga Ghat reopens after five days in Odisha, Bengal announces farmer compensation
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan recovery: Kalinga Ghat reopens after five days in Odisha, Bengal announces farmer compensation
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Odisha has restored traffic on Kalinga Ghat after a five-day cyclone-related closure.
West Bengal has announced Rs 212.3 crore in preliminary compensation for farmers affected by heavy rainfall and crop damage.

Odisha: The impact of Cyclone Akvan continues to shape recovery efforts in Odisha and West Bengal, with road connectivity restored along an important hill route in Kandhamal district and financial assistance announced for farmers whose crops were damaged by heavy rainfall.
In Odisha, the administration has reopened the Kalinga Ghat road after keeping it closed for five days as a precautionary measure ahead of the cyclone.
Meanwhile, the West Bengal government has announced a preliminary relief package of Rs 212.3 crore for more than 5.73 lakh farmers affected by rain-related crop losses.
Normal vehicular movement has resumed along the Kalinga Ghat road in Odisha's Kandhamal district after the administration lifted restrictions on Sunday, November 22.
The road had been closed to motor vehicles from November 19 amid concerns over heavy rainfall, falling trees and possible landslides in the hilly region due to Cyclone Akvan.
The cyclone crossed the North Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coast near Gopalpur on the morning of November 20, bringing heavy rainfall and strong winds to parts of the region.
After weather conditions improved, officials from the concerned departments inspected the road to assess whether it was safe for traffic.
Following a clearance report, Kandhamal District Collector and District Magistrate Vedbhushan withdrew the restrictions and directed officials to remove the remaining barricades.
All categories of vehicles are now permitted to use the route.
Kalinga Ghat is an important road link between Kandhamal and Ganjam districts.

stories.headline: India, China hold 10-day talks to ease LAC tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
stories.title: India, China hold 10-day talks to ease LAC tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
stories.summary: The talks focused on establishing engagement protocols, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, and maintaining open communication channels
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India and China have concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh and putting in place measures to prevent friction between troops deployed along the frontier ahead of the onset of harsh winter conditions.
Sources in the Ministry of Defence confirmed that the closely guarded discussions, which began on November 8, 2026, a day after Deepavali, continued for nearly 10 days, with a short break in between.
The talks were described as cordial, though it remains unclear whether the measures discussed will be implemented on the ground before winter sets in fully.
Lieutenant-General Girish Kalia, General Officer Commanding of the Army’s III Corps, also known as the Spear Corps, led the Indian delegation.
The formation is headquartered at Rangapahar near Dimapur in Nagaland.
His Chinese counterpart and other military officers participated in the discussions.
An official from the Ministry of External Affairs was also present.

The latest round of talks primarily focused on establishing engagement protocols between the two sides, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, maintaining open communication channels and reducing tensions in the eastern sector.
Both countries have deployed substantial numbers of troops in the region.

The discussions assume significance as winter conditions along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh can become extremely severe, posing considerable challenges to troop sustenance, movement and logistical support.
Any delay in implementing the measures discussed could complicate the situation on the ground as temperatures fall and access to forward areas becomes increasingly difficult.
The second round follows the first Corps Commander-level meeting, held on September 6 and 7, 2026, at the Wacha-Damai Border Personnel Meeting (BPM) point in the Kibithoo sector.

stories.headline: Hyderabad on alert after email threatens to avenge terrorist Lateef Bhat's killing
stories.title: Hyderabad on alert after email threatens to avenge terrorist Lateef Bhat's killing
stories.summary: In response to a concerning threat email about a potential terror attack, Hyderabad police have stepped up security measures. The email, attributed to a group claiming vengeance for a terrorist's death, specifically named targets such as Hotel Tourist Plaza and Kachiguda railway station. While thorough searches have revealed no explosives, officials are diligently tracing the threat's origins and urging the public to remain alert.

stories.headline: Banks warn higher costs could hit demand
stories.title: Banks warn higher costs could hit demand
stories.summary: Mumbai: Impact of higher rates on demand and capital formation, banking sector liquidity, drought-induced asset stress and inflation risks were among the points bank executives discussed last week with top Reserve Bank of India (RBI) officials as part of consultations ahead of the December 4 monetary policy review.People familiar with the deliberations said that the central bank wanted to know whether a sharp rise in rates will significantly hit demand as it ponders on whether to hike the repo rate by 25 basis points (bps) or 50 bps when it announces its policy decision."Banks' feedback was that core sector growth remains strong for now but consumption demand will be hit if prices remain high as job creation remains a challenge and stress in some segments is showing," said a person aware of the deliberations.In the bi-monthly pre-policy meetings the central bank takes feedback from banks. Most of these meetings involve bankers giving their views and suggestions."The RBI wanted to get a sense on the impact of higher inflation on the ground. Then there was the routine discussion on banking sector liquidity and interest rates both short and long term. Though demand remains strong there were some concerns raised due to higher input costs," said a second person aware of the discussions.Indranil Bhattacharyya, RBI executive director (ED) in charge of the monetary policy department, and Sanjay Kumar Hansda, ED in charge of the departments of economic and policy research and financial stability, were part of the discussions besides other officials. Some bankers raised issues linked to the impact of drought in many parts of the country and also stress in sectors like gold loans.Farm Distress"Already, we are seeing some stress in rice growing areas where requirements for term funding have gone up and capital demand has increased as an after effect of less rains. Then there is some stress building up in gold loans which will be felt more by lenders who gave loans close to 85% of loan to value and now need more collateral because gold prices have dropped sharply. Some borrowers may let go of their pledged gold rather than give more collateral. All these factors will play out in the medium to long term," said a third person aware of the deliberations.India's gold loan market has seen a rise in non-performing assets (NPA) in the first five months of this fiscal, ET reported earlier this month citing a TransUnionCibil report.The NPA rose to 0.3% at the end of August from 0.16% seen as of March 31, 2026. Industry executives say that a high propensity of repeat borrowing with 27% of borrowers having four or more gold loans are contributing to rising NPAs.Outstanding gold loans reached a record ₹22.5 lakh crore in August 2026, almost thrice the levels of August 2023. Adding to the stress is the fall in gold prices which will change the loan to value calculation and add to stress. Gold prices are now trading at more than 30% below their peak.Banking system liquidity has narrowed to around ₹87,000 crore from a peak of ₹11 lakh crore amid various RBI measures, GST/tax outflows and festive cash demand.

opening: Mumbai: Impact of higher rates on demand and capital formation, banking sector liquidity, drought-induced asset stress and inflation risks were among the points bank executives discussed last week with top Reserve Bank of India (RBI) officials as part of consultations ahead of the December 4 monetary policy review.

People familiar with the deliberations said that the central bank wanted to know whether a sharp rise in rates will significantly hit demand as it ponders on whether to hike the repo rate by 25 basis points (bps) or 50 bps when it announces its policy decision." Banks' feedback was that core sector growth remains strong for now but consumption demand will be hit if prices remain high as job creation remains a challenge and stress in some segments is showing," said a person aware of the deliberations.
body: In the bi-monthly pre-policy meetings the central bank takes feedback from banks.
Most of these meetings involve bankers giving their views and suggestions." The RBI wanted to get a sense on the impact of higher inflation on the ground.
Then there was the routine discussion on banking sector liquidity and interest rates both short and long term.
Though demand remains strong there were some concerns raised due to higher input costs," said a second person aware of the discussions.

Indranil Bhattacharyya, RBI executive director (ED) in charge of the monetary policy department, and Sanjay Kumar Hansda, ED in charge of the departments of economic and policy research and financial stability, were part of the discussions besides other officials.
Some bankers raised issues linked to the impact of drought in many parts of the country and also stress in sectors like gold loans.
Farm Distress.
"Already, we are seeing some stress in rice growing areas where requirements for term funding have gone up and capital demand has increased as an after effect of less rains.

Then there is some stress building up in gold loans which will be felt more by lenders who gave loans close to 85% of loan to value and now need more collateral because gold prices have dropped sharply.
Some borrowers may let go of their pledged gold rather than give more collateral.
All these factors will play out in the medium to long term," said a third person aware of the deliberations.
India's gold loan market has seen a rise in non-performing assets (NPA) in the first five months of this fiscal, ET reported earlier this month citing a TransUnionCibil report.
The NPA rose to 0.3% at the end of August from 0.16% seen as of March 31, 2026.
Outstanding gold loans reached a record ₹22.5 lakh crore in August 2026, almost thrice the levels of August 2023.
Adding to the stress is the fall in gold prices which will change the loan to value calculation and add to stress.
Banking system liquidity has narrowed to around ₹87,000 crore from a peak of ₹11 lakh crore amid various RBI measures, GST/tax outflows and festive cash demand.

Banking system liquidity has narrowed to around ₹87,000 crore from a peak of ₹11 lakh crore amid various RBI measures, GST/tax outflows and festive cash demand.

stories.headline: West Bengal govt in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres in Singur: CM
stories.title: West Bengal govt in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres in Singur: CM
stories.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday said his government was in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres of land in Singur in Hooghly district, a day after Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar announced Ashok Leyland would set up a truck manufacturing plant there. Singur was the site of Tata Motors' Nano small-car factory, for which the then Left Front government acquired around 997 acres in 2006. The acquisition triggered a prolonged farmers' agitation led by Mamata Banerjee, following which Tata Motors moved the project to Sanand in Gujarat in 2008. In August 2016, the Supreme Court quashed the land acquisition and ordered that the land be returned to the farmers. "The West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) had been tasked with acquiring the 997 acres, and negotiations with farmers were underway to purchase the land at a reasonable rate," Adhikari told reporters. He said the government would "do something" with the land, without mentioning Ashok Leyland
